reconcile.note: Henry resolves the tension by distinguishing a distrustful demand for a sign, which Deuteronomy forbids, from Gideon's fleece request confirming a promise already made.

sides.snippet: You shall not tempt Yahweh your God, as you tempted him in Massah.
sides.verseText: You shall not tempt Yahweh your God, as you tempted him in Massah.

sides.snippet: if there be dew on the fleece only, and it be dry on all the ground, then shall I know that you will save Israel by my hand
sides.verseText: behold, I will put a fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if there be dew on the fleece only, and it be dry on all the ground, then shall I know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken.
